answer.evidence: The main body is a full-width (32 px) textured earth plane from rows 0 to 63. It is a uniform noise of tan and brown with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. The column scans at x=8, 16 and 23 show only scattered light and dark speckle, with no consistent band boundary. The only structure is the two narrow vertical wall strips at the left (dark) and right (orange) edges, plus a dark 1-2 row line at rows 63-64 that closes the wall bottoms. Grass tufts sit in the top corners. Rows 64-79 are flat ground in the same texture. There is no vertical south face of 3 or more rows, so the ramp reads as a continuous sloped or flat plane, not a standing volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's soil ramp carries about 5 lightness steps. The packed earth has speckled grain and horizontal step ridges. The side rails are shaded wood with a lighter edge and a dark brown shadow edge, and there is a grass lip at the top and a sandier base. Measured facts support this: 10 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown rather than black. The total palette is small (15 colours), but it gives visible texture comparable to the references. It is slightly less textured than the paving, but a careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking flat or sticker-like.
